headline: AI adoption in superannuation advice is growing but members still need human advisers for personalised retirement planning
reasoning: Michelle Lusty of Bravura Solutions notes that while AI can help superannuation members educate themselves and formulate better questions, it is not a substitute for personalised financial advice from a super fund's human advisers. She draws an analogy to medical advice — AI provides general information but may not account for individual circumstances. She highlights that recent government legislative changes (payday super, tax changes from the budget) are largely outside super itself but are driving greater financial literacy and focus on retirement planning. Her key recommendation is for members to use their super fund's tools and services, which are already included in their fees, and to make appointments with advisers rather than relying solely on AI.
quote: Will the member ask the right questions? Will their full circumstances be considered and oftentimes not? I mean, I think you would a bit the same way as asking for medical advice. Lots of information provided, but is it the right information for you? Should you really be consulting a doctor? It's a bit the same with your retirement savings. I think one of the real things for members to understand is that this super fund is a great resource. These services are already included and the fee for the members. And so to get on to their super funds website, look at their tools, educate themselves, use AI to educate themselves on what questions to ask, and then actually make an appointment with their super fund to use the service that funds are offering.
episode_title: How AI is rewriting retirement advice | the advisory
